newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in Thai float aftermath.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in Thai float aftermath.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in moderate early trading on Thursday in the aftermath of Thai baht flotation, dealers said.
They said trading was trapped in a narrow range, with focus seen moving to the band widening issue after the rupiah was briefly affected by the flotation of the baht on Wednesday.
One U.S. bank dealer said market talk of a dollar-rupiah band widening emerged again in the wake of the move by the Thai authority, putting renewed pressure on the dollar.
Dealers said band speculation emerged every few months in the market following a surprise widening in September 1996.
Spot rupiah was at 2,433.40/33.60 at 0300 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,433.0/33.5. Today was at 2,431.5/32.0.

The rupiah fell to a low of 2,445 on Wednesday on offshore selling on rumours of a baht devaluation. The rupiah recovered as Thailand announced a managed float policy although that was also seen as a de facto devaluation by analysts.
Dealers said the market shrugged off a possible spillover effect as economists hailed strong fundamentals shown by the country's latest macroeconomic indicators.

One European bank dealer explained strong rupiah support from the stock market point of view. He said portfolio inflows had also put pressure on the dollar, as reflected by the stock market index which has hit three record highs this week.
He said speculation linked to a band widening seemed to pressure players to buy put option on dollars in offshore markets.
Dealers said increased speculation of a widening was due to the Consultative Group for Indonesia (CGI) donor meeting in Tokyo later this month, to be chaired by the the World Bank.
The bank said in a report on Indonesia last month that some countries had a wider intervention band but did not specifically suggest that Jakarta follow suit.
But central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said it was not good sense to follow what other people were doing.
"This kind of argument is weak. That is not good economic policy that just because other poeple have 15 percent we have to go to 15 percent," Djiwandono said.
Dealers said liquidity was a bit tight at the opening, but seemed to ease later in the day. Overnight money fell to 11.5 percent from 15.5 percent at the opening.
Overnight swaps due Monday fell to 1.75/1.85 from 2.2 points. Spot/next was at 0.3/0.4 points.
There is no trade in value tomorrow due to a public holiday in the United States on Friday. Dealers expected the market to be quiet Friday.
One-month swaps were at 12.0/13.0, two at 25.5/27.0, three at 38.0/40.0 and six at 79.0/81.0 points.
The central bank set its intervention band at 2,427/2,619 and the conversion band at 2,427/2,475 on Wednesday.
